title: Restore Options — Cloud Copy Verified

fields.incidentName: Cyber Incident — EHR Downtime and Data Reconstruction
fields.from: ISO Marcus Hale, Forensic Firm Lead (SecureTrace Inc.)
fields.summary: The forensic firm has confirmed that the immutable cloud copy of the EHR database (ORRMC-SQL01 and ORRMC-SQL02) contains a pre-intrusion snapshot from 02:00 on March 3, 2026. The account used to access the EHR database was compromised via a cloned MFA token, likely through a phishing campaign. The on-site backup repository on ORRMC-BKP01 was deleted by the attacker at 05:12, but no evidence suggests the cloud copy was breached. The domain controllers cannot be assumed clean, because the intruder held an administrator account, and they will be rebuilt. The forensic team has preserved memory and disk images from ORRMC-SQL01, ORRMC-INT01, and the compromised admin workstation. The EHR downtime viewer BCA-VIEW01 holds the final good state as of 05:15 and continues to show that data. The ISO and forensic lead now recommend proceeding with the clean-room restore using the 02:00 cloud copy.

actions.text: ISO Marcus Hale and forensic lead confirm the cloud copy is pre-intrusion and the only viable restore point.
The forensic team completes the initial analysis of the MFA token compromise and logs the findings in the digital evidence vault (case ID: FT-2026-0303-001).
The ISO issues a formal directive to begin the clean-room environment build for the EHR database and applications, per CIRP-2026 Section 9.

planned: Begin clean-room environment build for EHR database and applications (02:00 copy)
Initiate domain controller rebuild and full credential rotation
Begin reconstruction of EHR data from 02:00 to 05:31 using paper records and BCA-VIEW01 packets
Schedule clinical sign-off by CMIO after high-alert medication and allergy data reconciliation
Confirm with EHR vendor that the interface engine must be rebuilt from scratch
issues: No clean restore point exists for the interface engine ORRMC-INT01; it must be rebuilt.
The paper record backlog (02:00–05:31) is 3h 31m; all clinical data must be manually reconciled.
The CMIO must approve the clinical use of EHR data after reconstruction; no restoration is complete until that sign-off.
fields.approvedBy: Dr. Elaine Whitfield, ED Medical Director (AOC)

instructorNote: This inject confirms the only viable path forward: restore from the pre-intrusion cloud copy. The AOC must decide whether to proceed immediately, given the risk of delayed care, or to wait for full forensic clarity — but the CIRP mandates proceeding with reconstruction. Watch for hesitation on the CMIO's role in clinical sign-off.
